title: requireAuth authenticates a key record with a missing, null, empty or non-string tenantId: req.auth.tenantId becomes undefined/null/""/a number and every scoped route runs its handler with that value
area: apps/api/src/auth.ts requireAuth (no tenantId check); apps/api/src/store.ts:47 (returns doc.tenantId unvalidated)
evidence: Probe on 5350f68 through createServer + startTestServer, GET /keys with a key whose only scope is keys: record {scopes:["keys"]} (no tenantId) => 200, listKeys called with tenantId undefined; {tenantId:null} => 200, handler tenant null; {tenantId:""} => 200, handler tenant ""; {tenantId:5} => 200, handler tenant 5. Every handler filters Mongo by req.auth.tenantId; the mongodb driver serialises an undefined filter value as null unless ignoreUndefined is set, so a tenantless record could match documents whose tenantId is null or absent. Pre-existing, not introduced by this unit. Reach: schema/api_keys.schema.json requires tenantId (string, minLength 1) and POST /keys uses the caller's tenant, so only a hand-edited or corrupted api_keys document can be tenantless.
fix_direction: In requireAuth (the one choke point) reject with 401 when typeof verified.tenantId !== "string" || verified.tenantId === "" (and in store.verify), with tests for missing/null/empty/number tenantId. 401 is right here because there is no tenant to be scoped to.
reproduction: createServer(buildTestDeps({keyStore: fakeKeyStore({k: {scopes:["keys"]}}), keys: <listKeys records its tenantId argument>})); fetch GET /keys with Authorization: Bearer k => 200 and listKeys(undefined).
